Eileen: quick FYI — discovered another SDK parity snag affecting function-calling fixtures in samplekit. Node validator treats missing optional fields as absent, python json_mode is filling them with `null` and our schema has `default` for some fields so node will end up with the default while python stays null. Repro: 

Eileen: ```bash
# fixture: fixtures/fncall_missing_field.json (toolOutput has no `confidence` key)
# node (passes)
npx redwood-sample lint --schema schemas/fncall.json fixtures/fncall_missing_field.json
# python (fails under json_mode)
python -m redwood_samplekit lint --schema schemas/fncall.json fixtures/fncall_missing_field.json --json-mode
```

Vik: paste error?

Eileen: error snippet: 
```
ValidationError: At path "tool_output.confidence": null is not of type 'number'
  while schema allows a numeric default of 0.95 when the key is absent
```

Noah: hmm. Node's pipeline apparently applies `schema-defaults` transform (we added that in the node helper last year) so absent -> default before validation. Python jsonschema doesn't mutate input by default and `null` is considered an explicit present value that won't be replaced by defaults. So parity gap.

Vik: why is python seeing `null` instead of absent? Is the fixture generator or a retry wrapper injecting nulls?

Eileen: looks like the python SDK helper that sanitizes function outputs to ensure stable shapes inserts `null` for any missing key during parsing (it was meant to make downstream code simpler). Node didn't have that behavior. So two orthogonal differences: node applies defaults, python inserts nulls. Together they cause failures or divergent normalized objects.

Noah: customer impact: quickstarts that assert canonical objects fail CI for python users and produce confusing lint errors. New devs hit this during sample-app exercises.

Vik: proposed solutions: (1) remove the python helper that inserts nulls (breaking change risk), (2) make python helper opt-in behind `--fill-missing-with-null` flag and add `--apply-schema-defaults` to symmetry with node, (3) canonicalize sample fixtures to be explicit — include the default fields in fixtures.

Eileen: for immediacy I'm going to update samplekit fixtures to explicitly include `confidence: 0.95` where expected. Long-term we should align the SDKs. I prefer adding an explicit `--apply-schema-defaults` flag to python lint that runs a non-destructive defaults pass (only when key absent) so `null` remains an error and present values are respected. That mirrors node but keeps behavior explicit.

Noah: agree. Also add a lint-mode matrix test: run node lint, python lint with `--apply-schema-defaults`, and python lint without it; assert node == python-with-flag and python-without-flag errors as expected. That will stop regressions.

Vik: I'll open a PR to remove the implicit null-filling behavior in the next SDK major and make it opt-in during the patch so we don't surprise users. For now a samplekit fixture change + python CLI flag is safest.

ci-bot: PR 7342 opened by Vik  draft: https://ci.redwood.ai/pr/7342 (unit tests pending)

QA-bot: Added test plan ticket: TEST-2982 "SDK parity: schema defaults vs null-fill behavior". Marking regression risk HIGH for onboarding flows.

Eileen: thanks. I'll also add a short note in the quickstart: "Why lint may differ between Node and Python" and list three parity items: defaults application, null vs absent handling, and json-string parsing heuristics.

Noah: good. After the flag lands let's run the bootcamp fixtures across both SDKs for the last 6 months of commits to be sure we didn't miss edgecases.

Vik: will schedule a short eng-sync with eng-ml validators to make sure server-side transforms don't diverge too.

Eileen: will push samplekit fixture patch now to unblock incoming bootcamps. Thanks all.
